findings.observation: Reviewed CC Application Section 10, which confirms the site is subject to Compatibility Standards (checkbox marked 'Yes'). Examined Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan) blocks.md and used vision tool to analyze the sheet. Sheet 14 clearly shows adjacent properties with both zoning designations AND actual land uses labeled. Examples include: properties to the west labeled 'ZONING: SF-3, USE: SINGLE FAMILY' and 'ZONING: MF-3, USE: APARTMENT/CONDO'; property to the south labeled 'ZONING: SF-3, USE: SF-RES'. Sheet 13 (Overall Site Plan) also shows adjacent lots with zoning designations (CS, CS-V, CS-MU-V-CO, SF-3).
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a 'land use map showing adjacent land uses' when subject to Compatibility Standards. Since the site is confirmed to be subject to these standards, this item applies. Sheet 14 provides a comprehensive site plan that labels adjacent properties with both their zoning designations and actual uses (e.g., 'SINGLE FAMILY', 'APARTMENT/CONDO', 'SF-RES'). This satisfies the requirement for showing adjacent land uses. The vision analysis confirmed these labels are clearly visible on the plan adjacent to the site boundary, particularly for properties to the west and south that trigger compatibility requirements.
findings.explanation: Land use map showing adjacent properties with zoning and actual uses is provided on Sheet 14

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheets 35 and 36 guide.md and blocks.md files, which describe building elevations for all four sides (North, East, South, West). Used vision tool to analyze Sheet 35 in detail. The elevations show extensive architectural elements including: windows and glazing with detailed mullion patterns, doors (entry doors, garage entries, sliding doors to balconies), balconies (both recessed and projecting with visible railings), rooflines with varying parapet heights, awnings/canopies, and amenity spaces. A Material Legend is provided identifying specific materials: Fiber Cement Board (Painted), Metal Panel, King Brick, Wood Tone Fiber Cement, Glass, and Living Wall. The drawings include material transitions, depth and shadow lines, individual window panes, and floor-to-floor elevation heights.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires building elevations showing architectural elements when subject to Compatibility Standards. The site is confirmed to be subject to these standards, so this item applies. Sheets 35 and 36 provide detailed architectural elevations for all four building faces, going well beyond simple outlines. The vision analysis confirmed that the elevations show substantive architectural features including materials, fenestration, balconies, doors, rooflines, and other building elements with a comprehensive material legend. This level of detail satisfies the completeness check requirement for showing architectural elements on building elevations.
findings.explanation: Building elevations for all four sides with detailed architectural elements and material legend provided on Sheets 35-36

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 14 guide.md and blocks.md, which describe a Compatibility Setback Lines table. Used vision tool to analyze Sheet 14 in detail. The plan clearly shows compatibility setback lines radiating inward from the southern property line where it borders the SF-3 zoned lot. Four dashed lines are labeled: '15' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', '25' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', '50' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', and '75' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE'. A table on the sheet defines the zones: 0'-15' allows 0' height (SCREENING ZONE), 15'-25' allows 0' height (RESTRICTED ZONE), 25'-50' allows 40' height, 50'-75' allows 60' height. The setbacks are shown relative to the adjacent SF-3 zoned properties to the west and south.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires setbacks adjacent to residential uses or zoning to be shown on plans when subject to Compatibility Standards. The site is confirmed to be subject to these standards and is adjacent to SF-3 and MF-3 zoned properties (residential). Sheet 14 clearly depicts compatibility setback lines at the required intervals (15', 25', 50', 75') from the property line adjacent to residential properties. The accompanying table specifies allowable building heights within each zone. The vision analysis confirmed these setback lines are clearly drawn and labeled on the site plan, particularly where the site borders the triggering SF-3 properties. This satisfies the completeness check requirement for showing setbacks adjacent to residential uses.
findings.explanation: Compatibility setback lines at 15', 25', 50', and 75' intervals shown on Sheet 14 with accompanying height restriction table

summary: All 3 items pass. The site is subject to Compatibility Standards, and all required documentation is provided: land use map showing adjacent uses (Sheet 14), building elevations with architectural elements (Sheets 35-36), and compatibility setback lines (Sheet 14).
